title: Efficient Feistel Recovery at the Near-Linear Sample Boundary
summary: Exhaustive search is the known recovery baseline, and no efficient generic recovery method is known at the information-theoretic sample boundary, leaving that regime unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a balanced Feistel network, does there exist a generic efficient attack, polynomial in $N$, that recovers the round functions from $q \sim N$ known plaintext/ciphertext samples? Exhaustive search can recover all functions in time $N^{O(N)}$, while no efficient generic attack polynomial in $N$ is known in the $q \sim N$ regime.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis and generic attack complexity for balanced Feistel networks.
parameters: N: size parameter governing polynomial-time efficiency
q: number of known plaintext/ciphertext samples, with q approximately N
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a generic efficient attack polynomial in N can recover the round functions from approximately N known plaintext/ciphertext samples.

citations.label: Breaking the FF3 Format-Preserving Encryption Standard over Small Domains

progress.summary: The source gives exhaustive search as a recovery baseline and states that no efficient generic attack polynomial in N is known in the approximately N-sample regime.
